Subject: Stakeholder mapping & champion enablement — next steps (Finovate)

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the time today — really useful call and excited about the potential fit between Finovate and Redwood. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary use case: real-time customer support summarization + dynamic knowledge reranking for chat agents.
- Target SLA: 200ms p50 for short responses; batch embedding jobs for nightly index refresh.
- Compliance needs: SOC 2 evidence, customer-managed keys (KMS), and IP/data segregation for regulated products.
- Expected Q4 pilot: 2 teams, ~10K monthly active conversations, runway to expand in H1.

Requested next steps:
1) Stakeholder map — who are the economic buyer, procurement/security contacts, and the executive sponsor we should be working with? If you can share names/emails, I’ll prepare tailored materials for each.
2) Procurement checklist — curious about any standard PoC procurement hurdles (PO, security questionnaire timelines, legal redlines).
3) Champion enablement — I’ll put together a short internal slide deck & talk track for Alex and the product team to help drive the internal conversation.

I’ve attached a short champion deck draft and a template for stakeholder mapping — feel free to edit. I’m looping Dylan (SE) on this thread to help with any technical follow-ups and Neha (CS) to align on success metrics for the pilot.

Proposed timing: if you can share the stakeholder list by EOW (Friday), we can get a tailored ROI slide and procurement summary ready for your procurement meeting next week.

Thanks again — and happy to jump on a 20m follow-up if that’s easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches what we heard internally. Quick answers and a few asks: 

Stakeholder map (high level):
- Economic buyer: Alex Rios (SVP Product) — alex.rios@finovate.com
- Executive sponsor/champion: Priya Menon (Head of Customer Ops) — priya@finovate.com

- Procurement contact: procurement@finovate.com (we use a shared mailbox; Sam from procurement will lead)

Procurement/security timeline:
- Security questionnaire & initial SOC 2 docs needed — target 2 weeks for first pass.
- Legal: standard SaaS MSAs, but we usually request a 60-day review window.
- Procurement needs: preliminary pricing for a 3-month pilot and an estimate of expected token/embedding usage for budgeting.

Can you please: 
1) Send a one-page ROI estimate we can include with the procurement request (high-level cost vs. expected agent efficiency uplift).
2) Provide a short talking points doc (2‑3 bullets) for Alex that highlights the business impact and timing (pilot -> expansion).
3) Confirm what SOC 2 artifacts you can share immediately and which items require legal/contract sign-off.

I’ve attached our RFP template with the standard procurement items — can you review and flag any hard stops?

Thanks — I’ll share internally and loop Sam from procurement if we need to get formal approvals.

Best,
Priya Menon

Thanks Priya — this is perfect. Attaching the one-pager ROI estimate and a 2-slide talk track for Alex. Below are the quick answers to your SOC / procurement questions.

SOC 2 & security artifacts:
- Immediate: SOC 2 Type II summary report (redacted) + security whitepaper + encryption/KMS architecture doc. These are fine to share with security for initial review.
- After NDA / contractual acceptance: Full SOC 2 report, penetration test reports, and customer-specific architecture diagrams.

Procurement asks: 
- Pilot pricing: we propose a 3-month pilot at a reduced unit price with a capped token spend estimate. Draft pricing included in the ROI one-pager.
- Usage estimate: based on your expected 10K monthly active conversations, we model ~2.2M tokens/month and nightly embedding jobs of ~1.5M vectors — Dylan can refine this with you if you share sample conversation lengths/distribution.

Attached deliverables: 
- redwood_champion_deck.pdf (2 slides: executive talking points + champion enablement checklist)
- redwood_roi_onepager.pdf (one-page cost vs. benefit, pilot pricing)

Dylan — can you validate the usage numbers above and add any technical blockers we should flag to Omar/Procurement?

Neha — happy if you want to add a short pilot success metric we can include (CS perspective).

If it helps, I’m available for a 15m prep with Alex before he presents to the execs — propose Wednesday 10/14 10:00am PT if that works.

Thanks again — we’ll keep this lightweight for procurement so it moves quickly.
